{{short description|German mathematician}}
{{BLP sources|date=July 2020}}
[[Image:Hans_Föllmer_2006.jpg|thumb|Föllmer in Madrid, 2006]]

'''Hans Föllmer''' (20 May 1941 in [[Heilbad Heiligenstadt|Heiligenstadt]], Thuringia, Germany) is a German mathematician, currently [[professor emeritus]] at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin|Humboldt University]] of [[Berlin]],<ref name="Föllmer Schied p. ">{{cite journal | last1=Föllmer | first1=Hans | last2=Schied | first2=Alexander | title=Probabilistic aspects of finance | journal=Bernoulli | publisher=Bernoulli Society for Mathematical Statistics and Probability | volume=19 | issue=4 | date=1 September 2013 | issn=1350-7265 | doi=10.3150/12-bejsp05 | page=| arxiv=1309.7759 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Academy of Europe: Föllmer Hans|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/F%C3%B6llmer_Hans|access-date=2020-07-30|website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref> visiting professor at the [[National University of Singapore]], and [[Andrew D. White]] Professor-at-Large at [[Cornell University]]. He was awarded the [[Cantor medal]] in 2006.<ref name="Deutsche Mathematiker-Vereinigung">{{cite web | title=Prof. Hans Föllmer (HU Berlin) erhält die Cantor-Medaille 2006 | website=Deutsche Mathematiker-Vereinigung | url=https://www.mathematik.de/dmv-blog/15-prof-hans-foellmer-hu-berlin-erhaelt-die-cantor-medaille-2006 | language=de | access-date=17 December 2021}}</ref> In 2007 he became ''doctor [[honoris causa]]'' at the [[Paris Dauphine University]].<ref name="Hasani Hoffmann">{{cite web | last1=Hasani | first1=Ilire | last2=Hoffmann | first2=Robert | title=Academy of Europe: Föllmer Hans | website=Academy of Europe | url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Föllmer_Hans | access-date=17 December 2021}}</ref>

Föllmer is widely known for his contributions to [[probability theory]], stochastic analysis<ref name="Föllmer1988">{{cite book | title = Lecture Notes in Mathematics | last1 = Föllmer | first1 = Hans | chapter = Random fields and diffusion processes | date = 1988 | volume = 1362 | pages = 101–203 | publisher = Springer Berlin Heidelberg | issn = 0075-8434 | eissn = 1617-9692 | doi = 10.1007/BFb0086180 | isbn = 978-3-540-50549-5 | url = }}</ref> and [[mathematical finance]].

In [[mathematical economics]], he made early contributions to the mathematical modeling of social interactions.<ref name="Föllmer1974">{{cite journal | last1 = Föllmer | first1 = Hans | title = Random economies with many interacting agents | journal = Journal of Mathematical Economics | date = March 1974 | volume = 1 | issue = 1 | pages = 51–62 | issn = 0304-4068 | doi = 10.1016/0304-4068(74)90035-4 | pmid = | url = }}</ref>

In mathematical finance, he made  fundamental contributions to the theory of risk measures<ref name="FöllmerSchied2002">{{cite journal | last1 = Föllmer | first1 = Hans | last2 = Schied | first2 = Alexander | title = Convex measures of risk and trading constraints | journal = Finance and Stochastics | date = 1 October 2002 | volume = 6 | issue = 4 | pages = 429–447 | issn = 0949-2984 | doi = 10.1007/s007800200072 | pmid = | s2cid = 1729029 | url = http://edoc.hu-berlin.de/18452/4274| hdl = 10419/62741 | hdl-access = free }}</ref> and the hedging of contingent claims.

The Föllmer process, a stochastic process first considered by [[Erwin Schrödinger]] but formulated in the language of [[stochastic differential equation]]s by Föllmer, is named after him.<ref>{{cite journal | first1 = Dan | last1 = Mikulincer | first2 = Yair | last2 = Shenfeld | title = The Brownian transport map | journal = Probability Theory and Related Fields | volume = 190 | pages = 379–444 | year = 2024 | doi = 10.1007/s00440-024-01286-0 | pmc = 11393018 }}</ref> In mathematical finance, the Föllmer-Schweizer decomposition is named after him and Martin Schweizer.<ref>{{cite journal | first1 = Masahiro | last1 = Handa | first2 = Noriyoshi | last2 = Sakuma | first3 = Ryoichi | last3 = Suzuki | title = A Girsanov transformed Clark-Ocone-Haussmann type formula for L1-pure jump additive processes and its application to portfolio optimization | journal = Annals of Finance | volume = 20 | pages = 329–352 | year = 2024 | doi = 10.1007/s10436-024-00453-6 | doi-access = free }}</ref>
